title: Bench graders cannot see the commands an agent ran
what: Give bench graders the agent sessions' tool calls (tool name and command, secrets never printed), from the session transcripts the bench run leaves, so a grader can say 'a Bash call ran python on a scratch file' as a fact.
why: 28 Oct, spec-met (a-spec-fix-is-marked-met-by-reading-not-by-runni): the rule 'the checker runs a sketch of a runnable failing case' could not be proven in 7 paid bench runs ($2.83): graders read only the final reply, the workspace and the ledger (agent starts, tool names, no commands), so 'a script ran' is graded by words in the reply ('sketch|scratch|script|скрипт'). Run 6 (rule on) found the defect by reading and the word grader failed; runs 4-5 (rule off) gave the same verdicts. Any rule about what an agent runs is untestable until graders see the commands (principle 5: a fact goes to code).
failing_case: evals/scenarios/check-runs-sketch on wt/spec-met: the grader sketch-was-run is a regex over the reply; a checker that writes 'I ran a script' without running one passes it.
pass_cases: A grader that asks for a Bash call running python passes when the checker ran one and fails when it only wrote the word.
No secret from the environment appears in what graders read (a test with a fake key in the environment).
